data.text:
SOTTO URGES PEACE, RULE OF LAW DURING PROTEST AT DISCAYA-CONTRACTOR SITE

Pasig City Mayor Vico Sotto on Thursday appealed for calm after militant groups and flood survivors staged a protest at the property of controversial contractor couple Pacifico and Sarah Discaya.

Protesters hurled mud and spray-painted the word "magnanakaw" on the gate of St. Gerrard Construction General Contractor and Development Corp.'s compound.

"I understand that we are angry and frustrated, but let's not resort to violence or acts that could potentially lead to violence or injuries," Sotto said, emphasizing concern for security guards, workers, and the protesters themselves. "Hindi naman yung mga corrupt ang masasaktan pag bumigay ang gate, hindi rin sila ang matatamaan ng bato. Nag-aalala ako para sa mga security guard, trabahador, at ralyista mismo."

The mayor encouraged continued advocacy for accountability and stronger institutions: "Don't feel hopeless... the momentum is on the right side now!!! Let us continue to fight for ACCOUNTABILITY, STRONGER INSTITUTIONS, AND THE RULE OF LAW. There are no shortcuts."

Sotto also assured the public that the local government unit will continue investigations, case building, and prosecutions—not only against the Discaya companies but also in coordination with at least five national government agencies. "Tuloy din ang mga criminal case at administrative action natin sa LGU concerns gaya ng illegal building structures at business tax delinquencies," he added.
